question: Why is consciousness described as fire independent of the means of knowledge?
premises: The great lord declared fire as the many-rayed one.
The state of consciousness is entirely independent of the whole set of means beginning with the knowable.
inference: Consciousness is called fire because it shines by itself, without relying on the apparatus of knowing.
plain_english: For this reason the great lord called fire the many-rayed one. The state of consciousness does not depend on the knowable or on any other means of knowledge.
